claim: NASA selected a Phase I concept combining thermophotovoltaic conversion with plasmonic spectral control for long-duration non-solar space power.

provenance.source_title: Plasmon-Enhanced Radioisotope Thermophotovoltaic Power Generation for Interstellar Missions
limitations: NIAC Phase I concept rather than demonstrated hardware.
Radioisotope architecture does not map directly to a disposable 10 mm SNS seed.
Target performance values are proposal goals, not measured results.
provenance.fact_summary: NASA describes a NIAC Phase I concept targeting more than 40 percent thermal-to-electric efficiency and 17 W/kg by combining high-index thermal coupling with plasmonic spectral matching.
provenance.inference_summary: Photonic spectral control remains relevant to larger host or relay power architectures, but this does not close rechargeable seed storage or packaged shadow-survival constraints.
provenance.speculation_summary: A heterogeneous SNS family may eventually use non-solar survival power on hosts while keeping scout seeds solar-dependent.
